title: Romans Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 12.

questions.question: In Romans 12, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Present your bodies a living sacrifice
Be transformed by the renewing of your mind
Having gifts differing according to the grace
questions.correctAnswer: Present your bodies a living sacrifice
questions.explanation: This command appears first in Romans 12:1, where Paul urges the brethren to present their bodies as a living sacrifice.

questions.question: What type of sacrifice are believers urged to present in Romans 12?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:1 specifically states that believers should present their bodies as a living sacrifice.

questions.question: According to Romans 12:2, what should believers not be conformed to?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:2 instructs believers not to be conformed to this world.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:2 say believers should be transformed by?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:2 emphasizes that transformation comes through the renewing of the mind.

questions.question: What should believers prove according to Romans 12:2?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:2 indicates that believers may prove what is the good, acceptable, and perfect will of God.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:3 say about how one should think of oneself?
questions.explanation: In Romans 12:3, Paul instructs believers to think soberly about themselves.

questions.question: According to Romans 12:3, who has dealt to every man a measure of faith?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:3 states that God has dealt to every man the measure of faith.

questions.question: What analogy does Romans 12:4 use to describe the body of Christ?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:4 describes the body of Christ as having many members, each with different roles.

questions.question: According to Romans 12:5, what are we as many in Christ?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:5 states that we, being many, are one body in Christ.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:6 say about gifts?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:6 indicates that gifts differ according to the grace given to us.

questions.question: In Romans 12:7, what should a minister do?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:7 instructs that those in ministry should wait on their ministering.

questions.question: True or False: Believers are encouraged to present their bodies as a living sacrifice.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:1 encourages believers to present their bodies as a living sacrifice.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 12 teaches that all members of the body have the same role.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:4 states that all members do not have the same office, implying different roles.

questions.question: True or False: According to Romans 12, believers should think of themselves more highly than they ought.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:3 advises believers not to think of themselves more highly than they ought to think.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 12 states that believers should not be transformed by the renewing of their mind.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:2 actually encourages believers to be transformed by the renewing of their mind.

medium.title: Romans Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What should one do if he gives, according to Romans 12:8?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 12:8 states, 'he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity.'

questions.question: What does Romans 12:9 promise will happen if someone abhors what is evil?
options: They will cleave to what is good
questions.correctAnswer: They will cleave to what is good
questions.explanation: This is found in Romans 12:9, where it states that to abhor evil is to cleave to good.

questions.question: What type of love does Romans 12:10 encourage among believers?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Romans 12:10, which encourages being 'kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love.'

questions.question: What does Romans 12:11 instruct regarding one's attitude in business?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:11 instructs to 'Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord,' highlighting the importance of diligence.

questions.question: What should believers do in times of tribulation, according to Romans 12:12?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:12 advises believers to be 'Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer,' indicating the importance of hope.

questions.question: According to Romans 12:13, what should believers do for the necessity of saints?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:13 states, 'Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality,' emphasizing the need to care for others.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:14 say believers should do to those who persecute them?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 12:14 instructs to 'Bless them which persecute you: bless, and curse not.'

questions.question: What does Romans 12:5 teach about the relationship among believers?
options: They are one body in Christ
questions.correctAnswer: They are one body in Christ
questions.explanation: Romans 12:5 states, 'So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another,' emphasizing unity.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:2 encourage believers to do instead of conforming to the world?
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 12:2 advises, 'be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.'

questions.question: According to Romans 12:3, how should one think of himself?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:3 states to 'think soberly,' indicating a balanced and realistic self-view.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:6 say about the gifts given to believers?
options: They are differing according to grace
questions.correctAnswer: They are differing according to grace
questions.explanation: This is found in Romans 12:6, which mentions 'having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us.'

questions.question: What is the attitude that should accompany serving the Lord, according to Romans 12:11?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:11 instructs to be 'fervent in spirit; serving the Lord,' indicating a passionate approach.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 12:12 encourages believers to be patient in tribulation.
questions.explanation: This is correct as Romans 12:12 states, 'patient in tribulation,' encouraging endurance during difficult times.

questions.question: True or False: According to Romans 12:10, believers are to prefer one another in dishonor.
questions.explanation: This is incorrect as Romans 12:10 states to prefer one another in honor, not dishonor.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 12:4 states that all members of the body have the same office.
questions.explanation: This is incorrect because Romans 12:4 specifically notes that 'all members have not the same office.'

hard.title: Romans Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 12.

questions.question: What should we do with those who rejoice, according to Romans 12:15?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:15 states, 'Rejoice with them that do rejoice,' which instructs believers to share in the joy of others.

questions.question: According to Romans 12:16, how should we regard those of low estate?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:16 advises to 'condescend to men of low estate,' indicating that we should not think ourselves superior and should be humble.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:17 instruct us not to do?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:17 states, 'Recompense to no man evil for evil,' emphasizing the call to respond to wrongs with goodness.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:18 suggest if it is possible?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:18 encourages believers to 'live peaceably with all men' whenever possible, promoting harmony.

questions.question: According to Romans 12:19, who says, 'Vengeance is mine'?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19 cites God as saying, 'Vengeance is mine; I will repay,' demonstrating that ultimate justice belongs to Him.

questions.question: What action does Romans 12:20 suggest taking toward an enemy?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:20 states, 'if thine enemy hunger, feed him,' illustrating the call to kindness even towards adversaries.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'sympathéo' in Romans 12:15 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Sympathéo' indicates a shared joy or empathy, aligning with the call to rejoice with those who rejoice in Romans 12:15.

questions.question: What literary technique is used in Romans 12:15?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:15 employs parallelism, presenting the concepts of rejoicing and weeping in a balanced structure.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of living peaceably from Romans 12:18?
questions.explanation: Psalm 34:14 advises to 'seek peace and pursue it,' echoing the call for peaceful living found in Romans 12:18.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the principle of overcoming evil with good in Romans 12:21?
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:44 encourages loving enemies and praying for persecutors, aligning with the principle of overcoming evil with good in Romans 12:21.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Romans 12:15?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:14 directly precedes 12:15, instructing believers to bless those who persecute them.

questions.question: What does Romans 12:3 say about how one should think of oneself?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:3 advises to think soberly, emphasizing humility and an accurate self-assessment.

questions.question: Which Greek word in Romans 12:9 means 'without dissimulation'?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'anupokritos' translates to 'without dissimulation,' indicating genuine love as instructed in Romans 12:9.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 12:21 encourages believers to be overcome by evil.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:21 states, 'Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good,' clearly instructing against being overcome.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 12:19 advocates for personal vengeance.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19 advises against personal vengeance, stating, 'avenge not yourselves,' reinforcing the idea of trusting God's justice.

theological.title: Romans Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 12:1 teach about sanctification?
options: Believers are called to present their bodies as living sacrifices, holy and acceptable to God, as a spiritual act of worship.
Sanctification is only an internal renewal without any physical or external expression.
The sacrifice of Christ alone suffices; believers are not called to any form of personal sacrifice.
Sanctification is a legalistic adherence to ritualistic laws to be acceptable to God.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to present their bodies as living sacrifices, holy and acceptable to God, as a spiritual act of worship.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:1 calls believers to present their bodies a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is their reasonable service, indicating sanctification involves a holistic offering of oneself to God.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 12:3 teach about human sin and humility?
options: Believers must think soberly and not arrogantly about themselves, recognizing that faith is a gift from God.
It teaches that believers should boast in their spiritual gifts to elevate themselves.
Human sin is overcome by ignoring humility and focusing on personal achievements.
Faith is earned by human effort and self-exaltation.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must think soberly and not arrogantly about themselves, recognizing that faith is a gift from God.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:3 instructs believers not to think more highly than they ought but to think soberly, acknowledging that God has given a measure of faith to each, emphasizing humility in light of grace.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 12:21 teach about overcoming evil?
options: Evil is to be overcome by doing good, not by retaliating with evil.
Believers must overcome evil by force and retribution.
Ignoring evil is the best way to overcome it.
Evil is inevitable and cannot be overcome in this life.
questions.correctAnswer: Evil is to be overcome by doing good, not by retaliating with evil.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:21 teaches that believers should not be overcome by evil but instead overcome evil with good, emphasizing a proactive goodness rather than retaliation.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 12:19 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19 declares vengeance belongs to the Lord, reflecting God's attribute of justice in repaying wrongdoing in His own time.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 12:2 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:2 exhorts believers to be transformed by the renewing of their minds to discern God's will, reflecting God's call to holiness and moral perfection.

questions.question: How does Romans 12:4-5 connect to the broader biblical theme of the Church as the Body of Christ?
options: It illustrates the unity and diversity in the Church, fulfilling Christ’s teaching that believers are one body with many members.
It emphasizes individualism over corporate identity in the Church.
It teaches that only one spiritual gift is necessary for the Church's function.
It denies any interdependence among believers.
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the unity and diversity in the Church, fulfilling Christ’s teaching that believers are one body with many members.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:4-5 uses the metaphor of many members in one body to teach the unity and diversity of the Church, a theme consistent with 1 Corinthians 12.

questions.question: How does Romans 12:14-15 prepare for the New Testament ethic of love and suffering found in 1 Peter?
options: It commands blessing persecutors and empathizing with others’ joys and sorrows, anticipating the New Testament call to suffer for righteousness’ sake with love.
It encourages retaliation against persecutors to defend the faith.
It promotes indifference to the suffering of others.
It limits love to only those who are kind to us.
questions.correctAnswer: It commands blessing persecutors and empathizing with others’ joys and sorrows, anticipating the New Testament call to suffer for righteousness’ sake with love.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:14-15 instructs believers to bless persecutors and share in others’ emotions, laying a foundation for New Testament teachings on suffering with love, as elaborated in 1 Peter.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Romans 12:6 and Romans 12:8 teach about spiritual gifts and service?
options: Diverse spiritual gifts are given by grace and should be exercised according to the faith and character with which they are bestowed.
Spiritual gifts are optional and have no real bearing on the life of the Church.
Only certain gifts like prophecy and teaching are valid in the Church.
Gifts should be exercised selfishly for personal advancement.
questions.correctAnswer: Diverse spiritual gifts are given by grace and should be exercised according to the faith and character with which they are bestowed.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:6 and 12:8 emphasize the variety of gifts given by grace and the need to exercise them faithfully and appropriately, underscoring the doctrine of gifted ministry.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 12:10 and Romans 12:16 teach about Christian interpersonal relationships?
options: Believers are called to brotherly love, mutual honor, humility, and unity of mind, rejecting pride and arrogance.
Relationships should be based on social status and personal gain.
Pride is necessary to maintain order among believers.
Honor is only due to those in positions of power.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to brotherly love, mutual honor, humility, and unity of mind, rejecting pride and arrogance.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:10 and 12:16 teach that believers must love one another with brotherly affection, prefer one another in honor, be of the same mind, and not be wise in their own conceits, emphasizing humility and unity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 12:17 and Romans 12:18 teach about Christian ethics in society?
options: Believers must not repay evil for evil and should strive to live peaceably with all men as much as possible.
Christians are permitted to seek revenge for personal wrongs.
Peace is not a priority in Christian ethics.
Honesty is secondary to winning arguments.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must not repay evil for evil and should strive to live peaceably with all men as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:17-18 commands believers to avoid repaying evil for evil and to live peaceably with everyone as far as it depends on them, highlighting a doctrine of peace and integrity.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Romans 12:19-21 promotes passivity in the face of evil. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Believers should not seek personal vengeance but trust God’s justice, actively overcoming evil with good.
Believers must ignore evil completely and do nothing.
Vengeance is to be taken by believers immediately and harshly.
The passage endorses retaliation disguised as kindness.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should not seek personal vengeance but trust God’s justice, actively overcoming evil with good.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19-21 teaches that vengeance belongs to God and believers must not avenge themselves but overcome evil with good, rejecting passivity in favor of active goodness and trust in divine justice.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 12:11 teach about Christian zeal and service?
options: Believers must be fervent in spirit and diligent in serving the Lord, rejecting slothfulness.
Spiritual zeal is unnecessary as long as one attends church.
Service should be casual and without passion.
Zeal is only for clergy and not for lay believers.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must be fervent in spirit and diligent in serving the Lord, rejecting slothfulness.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:11 exhorts believers to not be slothful but fervent in spirit, serving the Lord, teaching the doctrine of zealous and diligent Christian service.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 12:8 demonstrate in relation to leadership and mercy?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:8 instructs those who rule to do so with diligence and those who show mercy to do so cheerfully, reflecting God's character traits of faithful diligence and joyful compassion.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 12:12 and Romans 12:13 teach about Christian perseverance and hospitality?
options: Believers are called to rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, continue in prayer, and be generous in meeting the needs of fellow saints.
Perseverance is limited to endurance without active hope or prayer.
Hospitality is optional and unrelated to perseverance.
Prayer should be private and detached from communal needs.
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, continue in prayer, and be generous in meeting the needs of fellow saints.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:12-13 exhorts believers to rejoice in hope, be patient in suffering, maintain prayer, and share with saints, teaching a doctrine of persevering hope combined with practical hospitality.

questions.question: How does Romans 12:9-10 fulfill the ethical commands of Jesus regarding love?
options: It calls for sincere love without hypocrisy and brotherly affection that prefers others, aligning with Jesus’ command to love one another.
It permits love only for those who reciprocate it.
It teaches love as a mere feeling without action.
questions.correctAnswer: It calls for sincere love without hypocrisy and brotherly affection that prefers others, aligning with Jesus’ command to love one another.
questions.explanation: Romans 12:9-10 requires love without dissimulation and brotherly affection with honor to one another, reflecting Jesus’ teaching in John 13:34 to love one another genuinely.
